newsitem.title: USA: Electric Boat still mulling joint venture.
newsitem.headline: Electric Boat still mulling joint venture.

text.p: Electric Boat Corp is still in talks with rival Newport News Shipbuilding Inc about teaming up to build a new attack submarine for the U.S. Navy, an Electric Boat spokesman said Thursday.

President Clinton's fiscal 1998 defense budget proposes $3 billion for Electric Boat, a division of Virginia-based General Dynamics Corp, to join with Newport News to build four submarines over the next five years.
Under the plan, Electric Boat would design the submarine, and vessel construction would be shared by Electric Boat and Newport News, which is based in Newport News, Va.
The proposed teaming "is not a done deal," Electric Boat spokesman Neil Ruenzel told Reuters.
"Both shipyards are negotiating. We expect to reach resolution on the issues," said Ruenzel, but he gave no time frame.
"We are pleased that the defense budget supports construction of the New Attack Submarine in FY 1998 through teaming on the first four boats," Electric Boat said in a statement.
The budget proposes building one vessel each in 1998, 1999, 2001 and 2002.

"We are hopeful that the one-year construction gap in the year 2000 will eventually be rectified in order to support a more steady building rate," Electric Boat said. "This would translate to lower construction costs as the program moves forward."
Ruenzel said the teaming would be "kind of revolutionary."
"So it's important to let the two shipyards work out the terms and conditions of shared construction of what is arguably the most complex weapons system on earth," he said.
Newport News spokesman Mike Hatfield said the company had not yet seen Clinton's budget.

"However, we have confirmed for a couple of months now that we have been engaged in discussions with Electric Boat on a possible teaming on the attack submarine...However, there as yet is no teaming agreement," he said.
Asked when an agreement might be reached, Hatfield replied, "There is no way of predicting a time table. Discussions are ongoing and may or may not result in a teaming arrangement."
Electric Boat does not anticipate any loss of jobs in the event of a tie-up, Ruenzel said.

However, the company has said for some time that it expects its workforce to shrink to 6,500-7,000 by the end of 1998 from 10,700 at present. Ruenzel said Electric Boat has about 9,000 employees in Connecticut.
Industry analysts say the submarine partnership makes sense.
"The issue gets down to, with the budget still shrinking, what's the best way to try to optimize the industrial base out there?" said George Shapiro, an analyst at Salomon Brothers.
"Some kind of joint venture makes a lot more sense than an outright merger," he said

Michael Bunyaner, an analyst at Oppenheimer & Co, said, "The bottom line is that it's a good thing. Working together will eliminate the cost of competition and save the government upwards of $700 million, according to some sources."
((--Matthew Lewis, Hartford Newsroom (860) 727-0224))
